channel.title: Pier & Point · Irish Hill Playground and Irish Hill Corner Plaza
channel.description: Changes, corrections and dated milestones for Irish Hill Playground and Irish Hill Corner Plaza (Pier 70), San Francisco. Every item names its source.

item.title: Correction · Irish Hill Playground and Irish Hill Corner Plaza: Pier 70 Irish Hill Playground now records the Assessor lots it overlaps.
item.description: Pier 70 Irish Hill Playground now records the Assessor lots it overlaps. Source: DataSF Assessor parcels (acdm-wktn), lots 4110008A, 4120002, 4113001.

item.title: Correction · Irish Hill Playground and Irish Hill Corner Plaza: The record's text says Pier & Point, not 'the owner', where it names who read or chose the Assessor lots.
item.description: The record's text says Pier & Point, not 'the owner', where it names who read or chose the Assessor lots.

item.title: Correction · Irish Hill Playground and Irish Hill Corner Plaza: The record now says Irish Hill Park is a Port or Hoedown Yard developer obligation outside the 28-Acre Site (Port Item 9B), not the master developer's park obligation, and states the D4D's view guideline as written (elements located strategically, not 'kept low'). The map notes drop 'quarried away in the early 20th century', give the D4D's description of the outcropping, and no longer describe the map shape as two separate pieces or say the site is within Brookfield's site. The summary now says no source reports the park built rather than asserting nothing has been. Image credits no longer name design firms the figure does not credit or say 'adopted 2017'.
item.description: The record now says Irish Hill Park is a Port or Hoedown Yard developer obligation outside the 28-Acre Site (Port Item 9B), not the master developer's park obligation, and states the D4D's view guideline as written (elements located strategically, not 'kept low'). The map notes drop 'quarried away in the early 20th century', give the D4D's description of the outcropping, and no longer describe the map shape as two separate pieces or say the site is within Brookfield's site. The summary now says no source reports the park built rather than asserting nothing has been. Image credits no longer name design firms the figure does not credit or say 'adopted 2017'. Source: Port of San Francisco, Port Commission Item 9B staff report, 2017-09-22 (https://www.sfport.com/sites/default/files/Item%209B%20Pier%2070%20Approval%20092217.pdf); Port of San Francisco, Pier 70 SUD Design for Development, updated 2022-04-26 (https://www.sfport.com/media/8123/download?inline=).

item.title: Correction · Irish Hill Playground and Irish Hill Corner Plaza: The 2017 projection of $736,000 in annual Community Facilities District special taxes from Parcel K North and the Hoedown Yard, previously repeated on this record, is now listed once in the shared site-wide cost list for Pier 70, and this record points to it.

Source: Port of San Francisco, Item 9B: Pier 70 Mixed-Use Project approvals, 2017-09-22, p.16 (https://www.sfport.com/sites/default/files/Item%209B%20Pier%2070%20Approval%20092217.pdf).

item.title: Added · Irish Hill Playground and Irish Hill Corner Plaza: Irish Hill Playground and Irish Hill Corner Plaza added, built to fill the space between parcels PKS, HDY3, HDY1/2, C1 and C2 exactly. The event date is the Planning Commission's Aug 24, 2017 approval of the Pier 70 Design for Development that defines the spaces (Resolution 19980).
item.description: Irish Hill Playground and Irish Hill Corner Plaza added, built to fill the space between parcels PKS, HDY3, HDY1/2, C1 and C2 exactly. The event date is the Planning Commission's Aug 24, 2017 approval of the Pier 70 Design for Development that defines the spaces (Resolution 19980). Source: Pier 70 D4D, Figures 3.4.1 and 6.4.2 (https://www.sfport.com/media/8123/download?inline=); Port of San Francisco, Item 9B staff report, 2017-09-22 (https://www.sfport.com/sites/default/files/Item%209B%20Pier%2070%20Approval%20092217.pdf).

item.title: Milestone · Irish Hill Playground and Irish Hill Corner Plaza: DDA terms approved: the City may ask the Hoedown Yard developer to build Irish Hill Park, with costs paid from special taxes on the Hoedown Yard parcels and the Port's share of tax increment from the 28-Acre Site and Parcel K North; the Port's financing plan also commits its tax-increment share to Irish Hill Park if Hoedown Yard CFD funding falls short (Sep 26, 2017)
item.description: DDA terms approved: the City may ask the Hoedown Yard developer to build Irish Hill Park, with costs paid from special taxes on the Hoedown Yard parcels and the Port's share of tax increment from the 28-Acre Site and Parcel K North; the Port's financing plan also commits its tax-increment share to Irish Hill Park if Hoedown Yard CFD funding falls short (Sep 26, 2017). Source: Port of San Francisco, 2017-09-22.

item.title: Planned · Irish Hill Playground and Irish Hill Corner Plaza: SF Planning Commission adopts the Pier 70 Special Use District Design for Development (D4D) by Resolution No. 19980; the Port Commission's Item 9B staff report from the same period (approvals adopted Sept 26, 2017) names an 'Irish Hill playground' among the Pier 70 Mixed-Use Project's 9 acres of new open space (Aug 24, 2017)
item.description: SF Planning Commission adopts the Pier 70 Special Use District Design for Development (D4D) by Resolution No. 19980; the Port Commission's Item 9B staff report from the same period (approvals adopted Sept 26, 2017) names an 'Irish Hill playground' among the Pier 70 Mixed-Use Project's 9 acres of new open space (Aug 24, 2017). Source: Port of San Francisco, 2017-09-22.

item.title: Milestone · Irish Hill Playground and Irish Hill Corner Plaza: Port fact sheet describes Irish Hill, a 1.5-acre landform, as planned open space, with two development sites beside it to be rezoned with the Waterfront Site (~2013)
item.description: Port fact sheet describes Irish Hill, a 1.5-acre landform, as planned open space, with two development sites beside it to be rezoned with the Waterfront Site (~2013). Source: Port of San Francisco / SF Planning, 2013-11-26.
